transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-03
Start Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SRE) — Liam, Sara, Dev, Renee (Aventis)

Summary: short sync to nail down latency SLOs (p95), concurrency patterns, and propose a benchmark plan to choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we're Maya from Redwood, and Ethan and Priya are here on the technical side, can you quick do intros?
00:15 Liam: Yeah I'm Liam, CTO at Aventis, Sara's our ML lead, Dev runs infra, Renee on sec, quick note, we're on a tight timeline to decide by end of Q3.
00:30 Sara: Hi, basically we need to evaluate whether Redwood Hosted meets our latency p95 and also whether Dedicated or Private will be needed for compliance and throughput.
00:45 Ethan: Great, thanks. Do you have target p95 numbers we should design for?
00:50 Sara: For user-facing chat we want p95 first-token under 300ms and overall streaming p95 under 500ms for typical 40-token responses. For async batch scoring p95 < 1.2s. Also concurrency wise we expect 200 concurrent users at peak, with about 20% doing streaming calls — so ~40 concurrent streams.
01:10 Maya: That's helpful. When you say 200 concurrent users, is that 200 concurrent requests or sessions?
01:18 Dev: Usually requests, we run an edge that fans requests across internal workers. Peak QPS about 150 at 95th percentile, bursts up to 400 for short windows.
01:30 Priya: Ok so we should test both steady-state and burst. Do you have a preferred model family? That affects tokens/sec and kernel choices.
01:40 Sara: We're evaluating 7B and 13B families right now, want to keep cost down but need acceptable latency. We'll also try a quantized 13B int8 variant.
01:52 Ethan: Good, we'll include 7B fp16, 13B fp16 and 13B int8 in the benchmark. For quantized models you will see improved throughput but sometimes worse first-token latency depending on kernel warmup and KV cache behavior.
02:05 Liam: How does Redwood handle prefix/KV caching? We have a lot of repeated system prompts.
02:12 Priya: Redwood has prefix caching and KV cache reuse — automatic prefix caching is on hosted, Dedicated supports customer-controlled cache eviction policies, Private can plug into your KVS if you want. (transcription: "K V cash" sometimes in notes)
02:30 Dev: Any estimate for tokens/sec per GPU for those model sizes?
02:35 Ethan: Roughly on A100-like hardware: 7B ~ 2.5k tokens/sec single-stream throughput when batched; 13B fp16 ~ 1.1k tokens/sec; 13B int8 can get to 1.8k tokens/sec in good batching. But these numbers are very workload dependent — sequence length, batch sizes, and streaming policy matter.
03:00 Sara: Important: user experience needs streaming first-token fast — we care about tail jitter. p95 is key.
03:10 Maya: Understood. For Hosted we can provide verified perf profiles for our curated models, and we can run an initial benchmark ourselves. For Dedicated we can size reserved GPU pool to hit p95 targets. For Private you'd manage infra but we provide the runtime and optimizations.
03:30 Liam: For Dedicated, what's typical concurrency per GPU you recommend?
03:36 Ethan: It depends. For low-latency streaming, we'd aim for smaller concurrency per GPU to keep first-token low — maybe 4–8 concurrent streaming sessions per GPU for 13B, 8–16 for 7B. If you batch heavily and accept higher first-token, you can push concurrency higher — 32–64 for throughput-oriented workloads.
03:55 Dev: Our plan is 200 concurrent users, but only 40 streams at a time — so if each stream maps to a long-lived connection, we might need 6–10 GPUs for 13B to hit p95 targets if we keep per-GPU concurrency low.
04:12 Priya: We'll do capacity math in the POC. Also consider autoscaling burst capacity for spikes.
04:20 Renee: On security: we need SOC2 report, SAML SSO integration, KMS for keys, and audit logs. Private would be ideal for full data residency. Is SOC2 available?
04:35 Maya: Yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO certs. We'll share the compliance pack. SSO via SAML and SCIM supported; Dedicated and Private offer customer-managed KMS options.
04:50 Renee: Great — also interested in log retention and how PII gets redacted.
04:56 Priya: We can configure audit logs and redaction rules; in Private you control retention in your VPC.
05:10 Sara: Back to latency: can you do streaming benchmarks that emulate user typing (slow stream) vs single-shot generation? We see different behavior.
05:22 Ethan: Yes, we'll include three patterns: single-shot short responses (10–50 tokens), streaming slow-typing pattern (server-sent tokens over 500–1500ms intervals), and burst batch scoring (100k queries over 1h).
05:40 Liam: For p95 calculations, are you measuring downstream client merge delays or pure inference only? We want both but inference-only is priority.
05:50 Maya: We'll provide both: raw inference latency (service-to-model) and end-to-end (our hosted edge + network). For Dedicated we can also run in your VPC to measure real network.
06:05 Dev: Any gotchas with tokenization differences causing variable token/sec numbers? Our model preprocessing does a lot of prompt engineering, long system prompts.
06:15 Ethan: Tokenization and long system prompts means longer KV cache entries — prefix caching will help but initial generation costs more. We'll run tests with your sample workload to capture that.
06:30 Sara: Also, we need to validate that fallback policies keep app online if a model variant is unavailable — e.g. auto-fallback from 13B->7B without huge UX regression.
06:40 Priya: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants; we'll measure quality and latency tradeoffs in the POC.
06:52 Liam: Let's get concrete on benchmark metrics: p50/p95/p99, mean tokens/sec, 1st-token latency, median streaming chunk latency, and GPU utilization.
07:05 Ethan: Agreed. We'll output a latency heatmap, token/sec curves vs concurrency, and tail latency buckets. We'll also provide a cost estimate per-1M tokens for each deployment mode.
07:20 Maya: For timeline, we can run our initial benchmark within 48–72 hours once you supply sample prompts and an API key or test harness access. POC for Dedicated capacity can be kicked off next week if you want.
07:35 Liam: Sending sample workload today. Also price sensitivity: if Dedicated costs are within 20% of hosted per-unit cost with better p95, it's attractive.
07:46 Maya: Noted. We'll include pricing scenarios showing unit cost delta and recommended Dedicated pool sizes to meet p95.
07:55 Dev: A question — does Redwood provide per-route throttles and tracing to debug tail latency?
08:02 Priya: Yes per-route rate limits, tracing hooks, and token-level latency breakdowns in Console. We'll include an example trace.
08:18 Renee: About Private: for on-prem we'll need a shipping checklist for network (NAT, egress to control plane?), certs, and KMS integration points.
08:28 Maya: We'll send the Private deployment checklist. It supports air-gapped install options with an enterprise agreement.
08:36 Sara: Any limitations with streaming combined with function/tool-calling? We heavily use tool calls mid-stream.
08:45 Ethan: Tool-calls introduce blocking while tools respond; we instrument mid-stream pauses. We can simulate tool latencies in the benchmark. For p95 we should test with and without tool latencies.
09:00 Liam: Ok, let's agree next steps, and recap action items.
09:05 Maya: Recap: Redwood to run token/sec + latency benchmarks (7B, 13B fp16, 13B int8), include streaming patterns, provide heatmaps, share SOC2 & security docs, and pricing + Dedicated sizing. Aventis to provide sample prompts and access. POC kickoff tbd for next week.
09:25 Sara: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

Notes (imperfect transcription): "KV cash" typo in some lines, "Redwood Dedicate" sometimes said, "token per second" sometimes written as "token slash sec". Occasional crosstalk omitted.
